correctness.rationale: For fixed pinned vertices S, solving h_i=lambda(h_{i-1}+h_{i+1})/2 on each source-to-source gap with endpoint values one gives the symmetric hyperbolic cosine profile, with strict decrease of its minimum psi_lambda(g) in gap length. Deleting a source in a cycle merges exactly its two neighbouring positive cyclic gaps; therefore all one-source failures preserve the floor tau iff g_(i-1)+g_i<=B for all i. Summing k inequalities gives 2n<=kB, hence k>=ceil(2n/B); explicit balanced integer gap allocations of k positive parts meet all inequalities, including B=2 and k=2, while B=1 is impossible because each adjacent sum is at least 2. A closed-walk transfer on states g in {1,..,B-1} counts rooted length-k gap sequences, with n/k adjustment from rooted starting vertices. At B=3 and B=4 elementary integer-gap case classification gives the stated residue formulas. Independent subset/composition enumeration checked all n=3..12/B and both special residue phases; separately 2,746 exact rational Gaussian-elimination assertions compared the direct discounted Dirichlet solution after each source loss to the gap criterion for n=3..7 and lambda in {2/5,3/5}. These are bounded corroborations, not universal proofs.
residual_risks: A source failure removes only its pinned status; the vertex and incident edges remain in the random walk.
Requires n>=3, 0<lambda<1, 0<tau<=1, homogeneous unweighted undirected simple cycles; not multiple simultaneous source failures.

value.rationale: Robust source placement after any single pin loss is a natural reliability version of a recently defined discounted-hitting domination parameter. Exact feasibility, all optimal sets and a labelled transfer census hold across an infinite family for every allowable fidelity. The B=4 even-gap phase produces a concrete phenomenon not equivalent to the ordinary distance-one domination result. This is a motivated full family classification, not an arbitrary computation.
residual_risks: Only one lost pin at a time, and no classification of arbitrary graphs is asserted.

final_claim: For discounted hitting support on an unweighted simple cycle C_n after arbitrary loss of the pinned status of one chosen source, let B be the largest allowed gap length determined by the strictly decreasing two-boundary support profile at (lambda,tau). If B=1, no one-failure-resilient set exists. If B>=2, the exact minimum number of sources is ceil(2n/B); its optimal labelled subsets correspond exactly to positive cyclic gaps summing to n with adjacent gap sums <=B. The exact count is (n/k)[z^n]tr(M_B(z)^k), with explicit B=3 and B=4 phase formulas.
limitations: Unpinning is not vertex deletion or edge failure.
B is a parameter-dependent admissible gap cutoff capped at n; at B=1 the feasible family is empty.
